evidence: Graesse, Orbis Latinus (1861), index s.v. Irland: Hibernia
terms.comment: A large island takes a preposition, as a country does: in Hiberniam, in Hiberniā.
Not in Lewis & Short; a later formation from Hibernia.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 334.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio, geographical section, with the authorities it cites (cited as M-O s.v.).

J. G. Th. Graesse, Orbis Latinus (Dresden, 1861), German–Latin index, read in the scan at archive.org (the 1909 edition at columbia.edu could not be reached page by page); its forms are post-classical unless Lewis & Short has them.
